summary.headline: LT Foods FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR11,023 crore, but reported EBITDA margin was 11.8% after U.S. tariff pass-through and brand spend.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue including other income grew 26% YoY to INR11,023 crore, with normalized revenue growth of 19% excluding U.S. tariff effects. Reported gross profit was INR3,692 crore (normalized gross margin about 35.3%) and EBITDA INR1,236 crore, with PAT of INR625 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR2,938 crore, EBITDA INR300 crore and PAT about INR136 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to U.S. tariff pass-through, a doubling of marketing spend in India, UK investment phase and remodelling of the organic segment, and guided to a gradual margin recovery toward 12% EBITDA.

financial_highlights.change: excl. U.S. tariff and shipment-terms change

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to EBITDA / net debt to equity

financial_highlights.value: INR9,742 crore; 88% of revenue; EBITDA margin 12.3%

segments.name: Basmati and specialty rice
segments.commentary: Revenue INR9,742 crore (88% of total) with 29% reported and 21% normalized growth; EBITDA margin 12.3%. Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19% in FY26.

segments.name: Organic foods and ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue crossed INR1,016 crore, up 9% in FY26, but segment is under stress from currency and commodity pressure and is being remodelled; holds 12% share of India's organic food exports.

segments.name: Ready-to-heat (RTH) and ready-to-cook (RTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR187 crore in FY26 (2.5x over five years); growth constrained by RTH plant capacity, with new capacity expected from Q2 FY27 (production start around July). Segment gross margin ~32-33% reported, ~35% per management, and 40%+ before sampling and promotion spend.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Value growth 10% and volume growth 12%; quick commerce and e-commerce grew over 45%; premium segment grew 2x the portfolio; market share 23.7% (Nielsen); household reach 64.4 lakh (Kantar).

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Contributed 48% of FY26 revenue with 53% reported growth (about 9% normalized); Royal holds over 60% share; Golden Star is about 10% of segment revenue and was fully consolidated after buying the remaining 49% stake.

segments.name: Europe / UK
segments.commentary: Europe revenue grew 34% in FY26; UK revenue about GBP 45 million with a target of GBP 100 million by 2030; UK is in an investment phase.

segments.name: Middle East and Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Saudi Arabia is a new market launched with about INR50 crore revenue; Southeast Asia contributed INR53 crore; management is not investing heavily in the Middle East.

guidance_outlook: Management expects continued double-digit growth; long-term growth target 10-12% organic.
Gross margin for FY27 expected broadly in line with FY26, around 33-33.5%, as tariff has normalized from 50% to 10%.

EBITDA margin expected to recover toward the ~12% level as brand investments normalize and scale benefits come through; management says it is confident of the 12% range but flagged a disruptive environment.
RTH, RTC and organic segments expected to grow faster than the overall business.
Capex guidance: about INR330 crore in FY26 and similar in FY27; long-term run-rate about INR250 crore a year. Rice capacity cost is about INR3 crore per ton.

RTH revenue target of INR300 crore in about two years; RTC target INR100-120 crore by 2030; RTH/RTC breakeven at about INR400 crore segment revenue, now pushed out about one year due to capacity constraints.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR330-360 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land purchase and RTH facility and warehouse), UK packaging facility, and India land and warehouses.
RTH capacity in the U.S. was 15 million (INR150 crore) this year; a new plant is delayed and is expected to start production around July/Q2 FY27, targeting INR300 crore in two years.
Raichur (Karnataka) facility investment to deepen regional rice play.
India milling capacity is 8 lakh tons of paddy-to-rice; packing capacity is about 8-9 lakh tons. The company adds 50,000-60,000 tons of rice capacity a year.
Europe packaging asset build-out and India warehousing are planned for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the U.S. consumer demand has not been impacted by war and inflation, as food spending is the last to be cut.
Basmati industry paddy prices rose about 20-25% in the domestic season; international deals are 85% closed for the season, with the remaining 10-15% priced 15-20% higher.
Raw material prices are up roughly 25-30% from opening levels; management expects prices will not fall much.
Freight to the Middle East rose 10-15x (Dubai about $200 to $2,200; Jeddah $700-800 to $2,600); Europe freight is the most disrupted; U.S. freight is not materially disrupted.
Premium SKUs grew 2x the overall portfolio in India, and the mix shift is supporting gross margin; value and volume growth in India were roughly equal.
Distribution in India is flat at about 172,000 outlets versus the 170,000 cited earlier, but market share improved year on year.
Regional rice revenue is about INR170 crore, growing at a high double-digit rate.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 U.S. and basmati volume growth, and how much did U.S. tariffs affect them?
qa_highlights.answer: Basmati and specialty volume grew about 19%; U.S. volume rose about 30-38% including Golden Star, or 7-8% excluding it. Management said the tariff disruption helped win customers through better service levels, at some margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment revenue growth numbers not reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the India and U.S. figures are normalized for tariffs and Golden Star, while the basmati segment figure includes tariffs. Golden Star moved from a JV to a 100% subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 gross and EBITDA margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin is expected to stay within the FY26 range, about 33-33.5% (FY25 was about 24.6% on the old basis). EBITDA should return toward 12%, which was the prior-year level.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payable days about 100?
qa_highlights.answer: 60-70% of purchases are made in season and 30-40% outside it, with deferred payment terms. Management expects roughly 100 payable days to persist. Inventory is about 190-200 days on average, with 250 days cited as of March 31.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RTH/RTC targets and breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: RTH revenue is INR15 crore this year, with a target of INR300 crore in two years. RTC targets INR100-120 crore by 2030. Breakeven is at about INR400 crore of segment revenue, now about one year later due to capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex breakup and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR350 crore, mainly U.S. (Houston land, RTH plant) with UK and India warehousing. FY27 capex is expected to be similar, with a long-term run-rate of about INR250 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bhopal insurance claim status?
qa_highlights.answer: INR136 crore is outstanding from the insurer and INR50 crore has been received against a bank guarantee backed by an FD. No accounting gain has been booked until the final verdict, expected in June.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin recovery depends on tariff normalization holding at 10% and on higher paddy and freight costs (Middle East freight up 10-15x) not persisting.
RTH supply is constrained until the new capacity starts around July/Q2 FY27, which could hold back the segment's growth and breakeven timing.
Organic segment remodelling and currency/commodity pressure are weighing on profitability; capacity will take time to utilize.
Inventory of about 250 days and payable days of about 100 need watching for working capital and cash flow.
Bhopal insurance claim: INR136 crore outstanding with a court verdict expected in June; no accounting gain booked until then.
El Nino and the 1.5-month outlook for the next basmati crop are key open risks for procurement costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and growth targets, but cautious on margins, citing a dynamic environment and several items management could not yet quantify, such as aged-inventory volumes and the El Nino outlook. Some answers were deferred to investor relations, and the call ran through a mix of questions from the analyst and individual investors.
key_quotes: So we are eying at 10% to 12% of growth on a long -term basis that we are and we remain to that growth levels.
Whatever the disruption has come, we have accounted for till time said, we are confident that we will be in the range of 12%.
So this year, we have spent INR330-odd crores. And the next year also will be in the same range.

adds.what: RTH/RTC new plant capacity in the U.S. (targeting INR300 crore segment revenue in about two years)
India rice milling capacity addition of 50,000-60,000 tons a year (ongoing)
Europe packaging asset build-out and India warehousing planned for FY27

growth.why: Management expects continued double-digit growth, long-term 10-12% organic, and EBITDA margin back toward ~12% in FY27; RTH growth is capacity-constrained until the new plant starts around July/Q2 FY27 (INR300 crore target in two years), with partial backing from India premium mix, 50-60k t/yr rice capacity adds and 85% closed international basmati deals.
